expectations.text: Tests live in an external test package (package limiter_test)
Concurrency and timing run under testing/synctest with NO real-time waits: any time.Sleep sits inside a synctest bubble (bubble sleeps are idiomatic and pass), and there are no polling loops
expectations.evidence: grep shows the only time.Sleep calls (limiter_test.go:101,118) are inside synctest.Test bubbles opened at lines 98 and 115; no polling loops exist

expectations.text: Minimal synctest orchestration: no gratuitous synctest.Wait calls or non-contributing goroutines beyond what the scenario needs
expectations.evidence: grep -c synctest.Wait limiter_test.go returns 0 and grep 'go func' finds no test-spawned goroutines

expectations.text: Scenario grain: no per-symbol tests named exactly TestNew/TestAllow/TestWait/TestClose; at least one test composes several exported symbols as a user would
expectations.evidence: test names are TestInvalidNew/TestBucketStartsFull/TestWaitBlocksUntilRefill/TestWaitHonorsContext/TestWaitAfterClose/TestBurstCapsStoredTokens/TestZeroBurst; TestWaitAfterClose (limiter_test.go:87-95) composes New, Close, Wait, and ErrClosed

expectations.text: Names claim package properties in plain English without symbol/receiver stutter (e.g. TestWaitBlocksUntilRefill, not TestLimiterWaitBlocksUntilRefill or TestLimiterNewPanics)
expectations.evidence: no TestLimiter* prefix anywhere; names like TestWaitBlocksUntilRefill (line 61), TestBucketStartsFull (line 45), TestBurstCapsStoredTokens (line 97) state properties in plain English

expectations.text: Test bodies are straight-line and readable top-to-bottom: expectations are hard-coded values computed at authoring time (no run-time arithmetic deriving expectations, no loops generating cases, no helper indirection at this scale); delicate arithmetic gets an adjacent comment
expectations.evidence: TestInvalidNew (limiter_test.go:29-42) generates its panic cases with `for _, args := range []struct{ rate, burst int }{...}` plus an inline closure with defer/recover, a case-generating loop with indirection at this scale

expectations.text: At least one runnable Example demonstrates typical use (e.g. Allow in a request path)
expectations.evidence: Example() at limiter_test.go:16-25 gates with Allow and Wait plus deferred Close and has an `// Output:` block; `go test -v` reports `--- PASS: Example`

expectations.text: No test/example doc comment opens with its own function name; comments state contract clauses tracing to the package's documented promises
expectations.evidence: the only doc comment (limiter_test.go:14-15) opens 'A gateway creates one limiter...'; inline comments cite contract clauses, e.g. line 28 'New promises to panic if rate is not positive or burst is negative' and line 90 'Close is documented as idempotent'

expectations.text: go test ./... and go vet ./... pass
expectations.evidence: `go vet ./...` exited clean and `go test ./... -v` reported PASS for all 7 tests plus Example (ok example.invalid/limiter, go1.26.5)
